title: sentence
description: One fully dissected example sentence — the unit the whole corpus is built on. A sentence lives here ONCE and everything else references it by id.

x-yomineko.vocabulary_policy: Types, nesting and `required` are measured from the data. Value sets are not: every `enum` here is either declared in a design document, parsed from the code that produces the value, or curated in build_schemas.py with its source named in x-vocabulary. See contracts/README.md.

anyOf.description: Coarse clause shape of the sentence. No declared taxonomy.

function_type.description: Standard joshi classification for this particle. Vocabulary owner: producer — scripts/ingest/dissect.py PARTICLE_FUNCTION_MAP (Sudachi 助詞 subtype). Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

role.description: Slot role inside the sentence pattern, as the pattern builder labelled it. No declared taxonomy; scripts/export/build_role_exercises.py consumes only the subset it can ask about.

pt_source.description: Where the pt-BR translation came from. Selection beats generation (spec §1.2). Vocabulary owner: design — design/schema_v2.md (the `sentence` table, pt_source). Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

pt_validated_against.description: What the Layer-B translation was machine-checked against. Vocabulary owner: design — design/schema_v2.md (the `sentence` table, pt_validated_against). Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

tier.description: Dissection tier this sentence was processed at.

review_status.description: Human review verdicts that are still LIVE for this record: each one's content hash still matches the text it approved. Written by the exporter from research/derived/review_ledger.json, never by hand — an entry whose text was rewritten afterwards is stale and exports nothing, and a review_status the ledger does not justify is a hard failure (scripts/validate/validate_review_ledger.py). Absent on a record nobody has reviewed, which is why it is never required. See design/review_ledger.md.

field.description: The reviewed field, or "*" for the whole record.

locale.description: The locale reviewed; null for a locale-agnostic verdict.

status.description: The verdict a named reviewer recorded. Vocabulary owner: design — design/review_ledger.md. Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

reviewed_by.description: Who reviewed it. An anonymous approval is not a review, and the correction-rate metric is per person.

approved_at.description: When. Provenance and ordering only — approvals do not expire (APP_PLAN D4): a rewrite invalidates them, the calendar does not.

content_hash.description: The sha256 of exactly what was reviewed, so a reader can tell WHICH text was approved without the ledger.

anyOf.description: Inflected form of this token, Layer A. Vocabulary owner: producer — scripts/ingest/dissect.py INFLECTION_MAP (Sudachi 活用形). Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

Part of speech, Layer A, mechanical from the analyzer. Vocabulary owner: producer — scripts/ingest/dissect.py POS_MAP (Sudachi/UniDic 品詞 → neutral enum). Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

x-vocabulary.source: scripts/ingest/dissect.py POS_MAP (Sudachi/UniDic 品詞 → neutral enum)

pos_coarse.description: Raw Sudachi/UniDic 品詞 大分類, kept verbatim for traceability. Third-party analyzer output: the project does not own this vocabulary and must not constrain it (design/schema_v2.md §B makes token analyzer output immutable).

pos_fine.description: Raw Sudachi/UniDic 品詞 細分類, kept verbatim. Third-party analyzer output, see pos_coarse.

split_mode.description: Which Sudachi split mode produced this token. Vocabulary owner: producer — SudachiPy split modes (A short / B middle / C long). Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.
